battle.name: 十年戰爭
battle.theater: 古巴東方省山區至卡馬圭東部
battle.brief: 一八六八年十月十日，東方省拉德馬哈瓜莊園起義，揭開長達十年的獨立戰爭，至一八七八年桑洪條約收場。戰事集中於聖地牙哥、霍爾金山區與卡馬圭東部，起義軍以小隊游擊對抗西班牙縱隊。卡面這門一八五〇年的線膛野戰炮是西班牙砲兵火力核心，射程延長讓砲兵得以先於步兵壓制，起義軍只能以游擊應對。

kit.name: 線膛砲
kit.history: 線膛讓同樣的藥量走得更遠。砲兵第一次可以在射程上贏步兵。

countries: 交戰的兩方是西班牙王國與古巴島上的起義軍。一八六八年上半年，島上已接連出現未遂的武裝事變，招募的密使、軍火與款項在幾個月內湧入哈瓦那與聖地牙哥；十月十日，東方省亞拉地區的拉德馬哈瓜莊園裡，卡洛斯·曼努埃爾·德·塞斯佩德斯釋放莊上的黑人奴工並號召武裝，隨後霍爾金、卡馬圭與聖地牙哥一帶相應而起，起義軍在東方省山區站穩腳跟，組織出「武裝共和國」的雛形，與殖民地政府正面對抗。西班牙一方由馬德里任命、對殖民地軍政全權負責的「古巴總督」統率，軍事上稱古巴總司令，麾下是半島籍常備步兵團、古巴白人士兵與非裔「摩雷諾」營組成的志願兵，另有砲兵團、工兵、醫療隊與為數不多的騎兵，兵力由一八六八年不足一萬人增到一八七五年以後的八萬人上下。總司令更替頻繁，作戰風格也隨之反覆：一八六八年的縱隊在沒有嚮導的情況下深入山區，只換來疲憊與病亡；到一八七〇年代改用重炮、封鎖與「集中」政策，把起義軍壓回少數幾處山區，成效始終有限。起義方長期處於分割狀態，兵源是釋出的奴工、農民與城鎮青年，裝備以獵槍、卡賓槍與砍刀為主，缺少騎兵、糧秣與醫療。一八六九年海牙會議承認起義者的交戰方地位、志願者與軍火得以合法進入之後，海外支援成為隊伍壯大的關鍵；到一八七五至七六年，起義軍在武裝狀態下的總人數約兩三萬人，集中在東方省山區與卡馬圭東部，其餘省份只有零星游擊隊與地下組織。
countriesEn: The two sides were the Kingdom of Spain and the insurgents on the island of Cuba. In the first half of 1868 a series of armed attempts had already broken out on the island, and over the course of a few months emissaries, arms and money poured into Havana and Santiago de Cuba. On 10 October, at the La Demajagua estate in the Yara district of the Oriente province, Carlos Manuel de Céspedes freed the black labourers on the estate and called them to arms; Holguín, Camagüey and the districts around Santiago de Cuba rose in answer, the insurgents gained a footing in the mountains of the Oriente and built the embryo of a republic in arms to face the colonial government head on. On the Spanish side command rested with the captain-general of Cuba, appointed in Madrid and answerable for the colony's military and civil government, and styled commander-in-chief; under him served Peninsular regiments of the line, volunteers drawn from white Cubans and from the Afro-Cuban moreno companies, together with artillery, engineers, medical units and a small amount of cavalry, and the force grew from fewer than ten thousand men in 1868 to something like eighty thousand after 1875. The captain-general changed hands repeatedly and the style of the war changed with him: the columns of 1868 marched into the hills without guides and gained only weariness and sickness, while in the 1870s the government turned to heavy guns, blockades and the policy of concentration, squeezing the insurgents back into a few fastnesses, and it never worked. The insurgent side remained divided for most of the war. Its rank and file came from freed labourers, peasants and town youths, armed mainly with hunting guns, carbines and machetes, and it had few cavalry, little food and little medicine. After the Hague Conference of 1869 recognised the insurgents as belligerents and allowed volunteers and arms to enter lawfully, help from abroad became the decisive factor in their growth; by 1875 and 1876 the armed strength of the rebels was something like twenty to thirty thousand men, concentrated in the mountains of the Oriente and in eastern Camagüey, while in the remaining provinces there were only scattered bands and underground organisation.
people: 古巴一端最關鍵的兩個人是塞斯佩德斯父子。老塞斯佩德斯是哈瓦那省的甘蔗莊園主，青年時在西班牙當過軍官，經歷過一八三七年的卡爾戰爭與此後的流亡；他不像共和派那樣打算以憲法請願爭取自治，而認為殖民地只有在西班牙本土發生革命時才可能出現機會。一八六八年十月十日，他在自己的莊園釋放奴工並宣布起義，被後世稱為「國父的國父」。其子卡洛斯·曼努埃爾·德·塞斯佩德斯在十年戰爭中擔任武裝共和國總統，長期在美國與加勒比海沿岸募款遊說，一八七八年代表起義方赴桑洪談判。起義軍的戰場領袖以安東尼奧·馬塞奧最負盛名，人稱「青銅泰坦」，戰技經驗來自一八六五年的多明尼加戰爭，他把山區游擊戰推到極致，一八七六年六月在聖路易斯一役擊潰巴萊霍德雷率領的西班牙縱隊，其兄何塞·馬塞奧則在聖胡安山陣亡。馬西莫·戈麥斯自一八六九年起在東方省作戰，是起義方最長於野戰的指揮官；胡安·埃萬赫利斯塔·迪奧尼斯奧·克薩達以「孤獨者」之名，在一八七〇至七一年率數百人縱越整個東方省深入卡馬圭，後被捕槍決。約瑟夫·馬蒂是起義方的宣傳與外交核心，他輾轉於東方省、馬德里與紐約，一八七四年與埃斯特拉達·帕爾馬等人在紐約組織委員會爭取美國支持。西班牙方面，奧多尼爾侯爵率首批縱隊赴東方省並於同年病逝於哈瓦那；「古巴的棉花」杜爾切、「貓鼬」卡萊哈、推行「集中」政策的波拉維耶哈，以及最後促成停戰的馬丁內斯·坎波斯，各自分別代表這場戰爭的幾個階段，而卡萊哈以窮追猛打游擊隊聞名，維利亞特接手後不久便在馬德里自盡。
peopleEn: The two most important figures on the Cuban side were the Céspedes father and son. The elder Céspedes was a sugar planter in the province of Havana who had served as an officer in Spain in his youth, seen the Carlist war of 1837 and the exile that followed; unlike the republicans he did not mean to win autonomy by constitutional petition, holding instead that the colony could only find its opening when revolution came in the metropole. On 10 October 1868 he freed the labourers on his own estate and declared the rising, and posterity called him the father of the father of the homeland. His son Carlos Manuel de Céspedes served as president of the republic in arms through the Ten Years' War, spent long years raising money and lobbying in the United States and along the Caribbean, and represented the insurgents at the talks of Zanjón in 1878. On the battlefield the most celebrated insurgent commander was Antonio Maceo, called the bronze titan, whose craft had been forged in the Dominican war of 1865 and who carried mountain irregular warfare to its extreme; in June 1876 he destroyed the Spanish column of Balajodre at San Luis, while his brother José Maceo fell at San Juan. Máximo Gómez fought in the Oriente from 1869 onward and was the insurgents' most experienced field commander; Juan Evangelista Dionisio Quesada, the solitary one, led several hundred men in a march right across the Oriente province into Camagüey in 1870 and 1871 and was later taken and shot. José Martí was the heart of the insurgent propaganda and diplomacy, moving between the Oriente, Madrid and New York, and forming a committee in New York with Tomás Estrada Palma and others in 1874 to press the case in the United States. On the Spanish side the count of O'Donnell led the first columns into the Oriente and died of illness in the same year; the cotton of Cuba, Dulce, the mongoose, Calleja, Polavieja, who pursued the policy of concentration, and finally Martínez Campos, who brought about the armistice, each stood for a stage of the war, and while Calleja was known for hunting the bands down, Villate, who took over from him, killed himself in Madrid shortly afterwards.
kits: 卡面這門標為一八五〇年的線膛野戰炮，在技術上正站在滑膛前裝炮與成熟後膛線膛炮的交界上：一八五〇年代歐洲各國的野戰炮隊仍以銅製滑膛四磅、六磅與八磅前裝炮為骨幹，真正成熟的膛線野戰炮要到一八六〇年代才出現。它在這場戰爭裡的意義，是把西班牙砲兵從「射程上挨打」推向「射程上壓人」。西班牙方的砲兵是全軍最講究的技術分支：戰爭初年，古巴總司令部的野戰砲隊仍以舊式滑膛前裝炮為主，一八六八年之後軍備更新加快，線膛炮與後膛線膛炮陸續到貨，其中英國阿姆斯特朗廠製造的大口徑後膛炮配在哈瓦那與聖地牙哥等要塞與艦隊上，線膛前裝炮則分配給縱隊與前線砲隊，用來在遠距離先行壓制。起義方幾乎沒有野戰炮，只有零星繳獲的舊式小口徑前裝炮與極少數自行鑄造的短管炮，多半用於道路與隘口的伏擊，更多時候他們手上最可靠的「炮」是幾支獵槍。步兵方面，西班牙軍在七〇年代大量使用英國雷明登改裝的擊發步槍，並有七〇年制式步槍；起義軍的槍械是獵槍、卡賓槍、舊式滑膛燧發槍與自製散彈槍，另有寬身帶齒的「薩瓦萊塔」砍刀作為近身武器。運輸與後勤是西班牙的長處：全島鐵路把哈瓦那與聖地牙哥連接起來，沿海有蒸汽船，陸上用騾車與牛車；起義軍靠騡牛馱運鹽、玉米與軍火，並在山裡自闢路徑。騎兵方面，西班牙兵力有限，起義軍有馬卻沒有騎兵編制，靠馬匹逃脫與襲擾。
kitsEn: The gun on this card, a rifled field gun dated 1850, stands at the junction between the smoothbore muzzle-loader and the fully developed rifled breechloader: in the 1850s the field batteries of the European armies still rested on bronze smoothbore guns of four, six and eight pounds, and properly matured rifled field artillery did not appear until the 1860s. What the card gun means in this war is that it moved Spanish artillery from being outranged to outranging. Spanish artillery was the most technically refined arm of the whole force. At the beginning of the war the field batteries of the captain-general of Cuba still relied on the old smoothbore muzzle-loaders; after 1868 the rearmament quickened, rifled and rifled breechloaders came in, with the large-calibre Armstrong breechloaders built by the British Armstrong works going to the fortresses of Havana and Santiago de Cuba and to the fleet, while rifled muzzle-loaders were allotted to the columns and forward batteries to deliver suppressive fire at long range. The insurgents had almost no field artillery at all: a few captured old small-calibre muzzle-loaders and a very small number of home-made short guns, used mostly for ambushes at roads and passes, and far more often the best gun they had was a hunting rifle. On foot the Spanish army in the seventies relied heavily on percussion muskets converted from British Remington patterns, together with a service model of 1870; the rebels' weapons were hunting guns, carbines, old smoothbore flintlocks and home-made shotguns, together with the broad bladed sabaleta machete for close work. Transport and supply were the Spanish strength: island railways linked Havana with Santiago de Cuba, steamers ran along the coast, and mule and ox carts worked the roads; the insurgents carried salt, maize and ammunition on mules and oxen and cut their own paths in the hills. In cavalry the Spanish numbers were small, and though the rebels had horses they had no cavalry arm, using them to break contact and to strike from cover.
tactics: 西班牙的戰術主軸是「縱隊掃蕩」。每支縱隊由一千五百至三千人組成，配四至八門野戰炮與一隊騎兵巡邏，沿公路推進，由兩支以上縱隊對同一地點形成合圍，再以封鎖線切斷該區與外界的聯繫——因為起義軍靠山區與鄉村存活，公路與城鎮是西班牙能控制的部分。砲兵在縱隊裡承擔三種任務：行軍中以遠射搜索並驅散對面山頭的射手、交戰前先以曲射火力覆蓋道路與渡口、以及在扎營時以野戰炮封住縱隊兩側的出入。西班牙還用「集中」政策改變戰場條件：把鄉間住戶驅入鎮區，拆毀山邊的莊園與牲畜，企圖切斷起義軍的糧食與情報來源。起義軍的做法幾乎是它的反面：mambí 分散成十數人至數十人的小隊，白天在山嶺、沼澤與叢林裡休息，夜里趕路，專打縱隊的行軍縱列、單獨的補給驃隊與落後的哨兵，打一下就散，絕不讓西班牙找到決戰的機會。他們控制鄉村、奪取高地、破壞橋樑與道路，把西班牙砲兵的射程優勢一次次化解在近身衝鋒與碎步轉移裡。馬塞奧在東方省開闢的「馬塞奧小徑」正是這種戰法的延伸：一條穿過山區的畜力路徑，把糧食、鹽、藥品與人馬送到游擊隊的營地，繞開西班牙人守著的大路。奇薩達一八七〇至七一年的縱走則是它的極致，數百人的隊伍在山中穿行數月，深入卡馬圭省境，打亂西班牙原本的部署。到一八七〇年代後期，馬塞奧與戈麥斯把幾支部隊合成總指揮部式的集團，準備以會戰方式與西班牙縱隊對抗，但多數時候仍選擇在有利地形上打了就走。
tacticsEn: The Spanish tactical axis was the sweeping column. Each column was made up of fifteen hundred to three thousand men with four to eight field guns and a troop of cavalry outriders, moving up the roads, with two or more columns closed on the same point and a cordon drawn to cut the area off from the outside, since the insurgents lived off the mountains and the countryside and the roads and the towns were the part of Cuba that Spain could control. Artillery inside a column had three jobs: to search the ridges ahead at long range and drive off the enemy's skirmishers while the column was on the march, to cover the roads and fords with curved fire before the action began, and to seal the flanks of the bivouac with field guns. Spain also tried to change the conditions of the battlefield with the policy of concentration, driving the rural population into the towns and destroying the farms and livestock on the edge of the hills in order to cut the insurgents off from food and from information. The insurgent method was close to its exact opposite. The mambí dispersed into bands of ten or a dozen to several dozen men, resting by day among hills, swamps and scrub and marching by night, and striking at the marching columns of the enemy, isolated supply trains and stragglers, then vanishing rather than letting Spain find a decisive engagement. They held the countryside, took the heights, broke bridges and roads, and wore down the reach of Spanish artillery in a hail of close rushes and broken movement over broken ground. The trail Maceo opened in the Oriente was the extension of that method: a pack-animal path through the hills that carried grain, salt, medicines and men to the bands and bypassed the main roads Spain was guarding. The march of 1870 and 1871 led by Quesada was its extreme form, several hundred men walking through the mountains for months and pushing deep into Camagüey, disrupting the Spanish plan of deployment. In the later 1870s Maceo and Gómez brought several bands together into something like a general command in order to meet Spanish columns in a set battle, but most of the time they still chose to fight on ground of their own choosing and then move off.
data: 時間跨度是十年又四個多月：起事在一八六八年十月十日，桑洪條約在一八七八年二月二十三日簽訂。西班牙在古巴的駐軍由一八六八年的不足一萬人，增至一八七五年以後約八萬人；同一時期起義軍在武裝狀態下的總人數約兩三萬人，最多時接近四萬，其中東方省約佔六成。損失方面，西班牙軍隊的陣亡數在同期估算與後世研究中多落在一萬二千至一萬五千之間，起義方的陣亡人數一般估在兩萬至三萬上下，雙方數字都因游擊戰的性質而難以核實。財政是這場戰爭最沉的負擔：同期西班牙議會文件與軍事評論估計，古巴戰區每年耗費約二千萬至三千萬披索，十年合計逾二億披索，相當於西班牙國家財政的沉重一塊。經濟上，古巴的糖產量在戰前高峰約為年五十萬至一百萬擔，經過十年戰爭跌到三十萬擔上下，退回十九世紀初年的水平。距離與速度方面，縱隊每天沿公路推進約十五至二十公里，進入山區後減半；哈瓦那與聖地牙哥之間有鐵路相通，軍火與糧秣多走海路與鐵路，起義軍的運輸則全靠騡牛馱運，單程補給往往要走十餘里格。
dataEn: The war ran for a little over ten years: the rising began on 10 October 1868 and the pact of Zanjón was signed on 23 February 1878. The Spanish garrison in Cuba grew from fewer than ten thousand men in 1868 to about eighty thousand after 1875; over the same period the armed strength of the insurgents was some twenty to thirty thousand men, approaching forty thousand at its height, of whom roughly six tenths were in the Oriente province. On losses, the Spanish dead are put by contemporary estimates and later studies at between twelve and fifteen thousand, while the insurgent dead are generally estimated at twenty to thirty thousand, and neither figure can be checked easily because of the nature of a war of bands. Finance was the heaviest burden of all: parliamentary papers and military comment of the period put the cost of the Cuban theatre at something between twenty and thirty million pesos a year and more than two hundred million pesos over the ten years, a heavy charge on the Spanish treasury. In the economy, Cuban sugar output had peaked at between five hundred thousand and one million hogsheads a year before the war and fell to around three hundred thousand during it, back to the level of the early nineteenth century. On distance and speed, a column advanced about fifteen to twenty kilometres a day along the roads and half that once it entered the hills; Havana and Santiago de Cuba were joined by railway, and arms and provisions travelled mostly by sea and rail, while the insurgents moved everything on mules and oxen, a single supply journey often covering more than ten leagues.
cause: 打起來的原因分四層。第一層是西班牙本土的政局：波旁王朝在三十年代之後逐步退讓，一八六八年九月革命推翻伊莎貝拉二世，共和政府接手了古巴，卻無法壓制島上的抗爭；它對古巴採取的「自由派」姿態，推行自治與廢奴的說法，反而把原本支持母國的莊園主推向反對的一邊。第二層是奴隸制與糖業的經濟結構：古巴的糖產高度依賴奴隸勞動，母國與英美廢奴派的言論、加上英國在糖價上的競爭，使莊園主擔心廢奴會直接毀掉自己的產業。第三層是國際環境：美國在內戰後迅速把注意力轉向加勒比海，共和黨的擴張論者公開談論「古巴的前途」，而一八六八年十一月的大選與格蘭特政府的上台，使華盛頓的態度成為島上雙方都必須計算的變數。第四層才是直接導火線：一八六八年三月與十月的幾次未遂事變把散居海外的人、錢和槍械聚到一處，十月十日拉德馬哈瓜莊園的起義因此不是孤立事件，而是把此前所有準備一次性點燃；古巴知識分子自一八三〇年代起就主張，若殖民地不能自治，唯有分離。
causeEn: The reasons for the war run in four layers. The first is politics in the metropole: after the Bourbons had been pushed back over the course of the 1830s, the September revolution of 1868 overthrew Isabella II and a republican government took over Cuba, but it could not suppress the island's resistance, and the liberal tone it adopted towards the colony, with its talk of autonomy and emancipation, pushed the planters who had been loyal to the mother country into the opposition. The second is the economic structure of slavery and sugar: Cuban sugar depended heavily on slave labour, and the rhetoric of emancipation at home and in Britain and America, together with British competition in the price of sugar, convinced the planters that abolition would destroy their industry outright. The third is the international setting: after the American Civil War the United States turned its attention quickly to the Caribbean, expansionist Republicans spoke openly of the future of Cuba, and the presidential election of November 1868 and the coming to power of Grant's government made the mood in Washington a variable that both sides on the island had to calculate. The fourth is the immediate occasion: the failed attempts of March and October 1868 gathered abroad the men, money and firearms that had been scattered, so that the rising at La Demajagua on 10 October was not an isolated event but the lighting of every preparation made before it; Cuban intellectuals had argued since the 1830s that if the colony could not have autonomy, then only separation remained.
impact: 影響橫跨加勒比海與歐洲。對古巴而言，十年戰爭把「獨立」從一句主張變成一套軍事技術與一套外交手腕：人們熟悉了游擊隊的編組、破壞與補給方法，也熟悉了在紐約、巴黎與華盛頓如何募款和遊說。起義方雖未取勝，卻在桑洪談判中換得大赦與部分地方自治的讓步，海外的流亡者網絡與美國的同情也自此成形。戰爭把古巴的糖業與西班牙的財政同時拖垮，香港與紐約的銀行界開始重新評價加勒比海的資產，轉向支持出口港的建設，這條線後來通向一八九五年的新一輪起義，並最終捲入一八九八年的美西戰爭。對西班牙而言，十年戰爭是帝國成本的實物教材：它在本土催生一整套關於殖民地治理的爭論——自治、放手，還是加大鎮壓——也在軍事上推動了砲兵、軍制、後勤與徵兵的改革，一八七八年後湧回本土的殖民地老兵成為新政黨的骨干。國際法上，一八六九年海牙會議對交戰方地位的認定，確立了起義者可以受援、可以受條約保護的先例，影響了此後中立的英國與美國的軍火政策；一八七三至七五年的「維吉尼亞斯號」事件中，一艘美國船被西班牙當作海盜扣押，幾乎引起交戰，最終以一八七七年《華盛頓協議》收場。
impactEn: The consequences reached across the Caribbean and into Europe. For Cuba the Ten Years' War turned independence from a claim into a body of military technique and a set of diplomatic reflexes: people learned how to organise bands, how to destroy and how to supply them, and they learned how to raise money and lobby in New York, Paris and Washington. The insurgents had not won, but at the talks of Zanjón they bought amnesty and a share of local autonomy, and the network of exiles and the sympathy of the United States took its shape. The war wore out Cuban sugar and the Spanish treasury at the same time, and the banking houses of Hong Kong and New York began to revalue Caribbean assets and turn towards supporting the building of the great export port, a line that would lead to the new rising of 1895 and finally into the Spanish-American War of 1898. For Spain the Ten Years' War was a practical lesson in the cost of empire: at home it set off the whole argument over colonial government, whether to grant autonomy, to let go, or to tighten the grip, and in military terms it drove reform of artillery, organisation, logistics and recruitment, with the returning colonial veterans of the late 1870s forming the backbone of the party of reform. In international law, the recognition of belligerent status at the Hague Conference of 1869 established the precedent that insurgents could be aided and could be covered by treaty, and it shaped the arms policies of neutral Britain and the United States afterwards; in the Virginius affair of 1873 to 1875 an American ship was seized by Spain as a pirate and nearly produced a war, ending only with the Washington settlement of 1877.
result: 結果是雙方都沒有得到想要的東西。一八七八年二月二十三日，馬丁內斯·坎波斯與卡洛斯·曼努埃爾·德·塞斯佩德斯等人在加泰隆尼亞的桑洪簽下條約：起義者獲得大赦並可保留部分武裝，但一批領袖被排除在外；西班牙放棄對普拉特省西部地區的直接管治，答應日後逐步改革島上的行政與經濟制度，卻不承認獨立。條約簽訂後幾個月，東南部就爆發「小戰」，卡馬圭與拉斯圖納斯一帶的游擊重燃；一八七九年塞斯佩德斯回到島上組閣，一八八〇年馬德里的阿方索十二世政府則以更嚴厲的手段回應，島上的游擊隊伍一直延續到一八八〇年代中期仍未完全清剿。因此這場戰爭的結局，是西班牙在法律上重新控制古巴，實控力卻大為削弱；起義方失去了戰爭，得到了經驗、人脈與國際同情。馬塞奧沒有在這十年裡陣亡，他帶著隊伍走過一八七九至八六年的沉寂，直到一八九五年第三次起義時再度出山，並於一八九六年在聖佩德羅一帶傷重身亡。真正的勝負，要到下一場戰爭才見分曉。
resultEn: The result was that neither side got what it wanted. On 23 February 1878 Martínez Campos and Carlos Manuel de Céspedes, with others, signed the pact at Zanjón in Catalonia: the insurgents received amnesty and were allowed to keep part of their arms, but a number of the leaders were excluded; Spain gave up direct government of the western districts of the province of Puerto Príncipe and promised gradual reform of the island's administration and economy, while recognising no independence. Within months of the signing the small war broke out again in the east, bands reviving in Camagüey and Las Tunas, Céspedes returning to the island in 1879 to form a cabinet, and Madrid under Alfonso XII answering with harsher measures; the bands on the island were not fully cleared up until the middle of the 1880s. So the war ended with Spain legally in control of Cuba and much less effective control in practice, while the insurgents lost the war and gained experience, connections and international sympathy. Maceo did not fall in those ten years: he led his men through the quiet years of 1879 to 1886 and came back out for the third rising of 1895, dying of his wounds at San Pedro in 1896. The real verdict was not delivered until the next war.
